question: The waste-water treatment plant (WWTP) Rincón de León serves the municipalities of Alicante and San Vicente del Raspeig. As many groups have been denouncing for over 20 years, the WWTP has been discharging untreated waters into the Natura 2000 site SCI/SPA ES0000214 – ‘Espacio Marino de Tabarca’.

These discharges of urban and industrial waste waters have been found to contain heavy metals, phenols, other hydrocarbons, fats and various kinds of toxic substances, causing serious damage by polluting protected habitats, such as posidonia meadows, and a significant loss of marine biodiversity, in addition to the danger to human health.

In a number of complaints to the courts and to this Commission, the Gran Via Sur Puerto neighbourhood association has pointed to the connivance of the competent authorities in the mismanagement of discharges and the irreversible damage caused to beaches such as the one in San Gabriel, in the El Cocó area, in the port docks, with several discharge points and, in particular, in the SCI/SPA ES0000214 – ‘Espacio Marino de Tabarca’.
Does the Commission intend to take action to prevent any further degradation of SCI/SPA ES0000214 – ‘Espacio Marino de Tabarca’?
What measures will the Commission take to ensure that the local authorities in Alicante act diligently with regard to the treatment of discharges?
answer: 1. In Natura 2000 sites, like ‘Espacio Marino de Tabarca’, the Habitats Directive (1) requires Member States to avoid deterioration of natural habitats and significant disturbance of related species. Without prejudice to the Commission’s role as guardian of Treaties, Member States are primarily responsible of compliance with their obligations under EU law.

In line with its implementation of EU law’s mission (2), the Commission monitors the implementation of this directive by Spain. As Spain failed to designate Sites of Community Importance as Special Areas of Conservation (SAC) and set-up specific conservation objectives and measures in SAC, like ‘Espacio Marino de Tabarca’, the Commission decided to open an infringement procedure in 2015 (3).

In July 2020, the Commission sent an additional letter of formal notice to Spain. 2. According to the last Report (2020) under the Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive (4), the agglomeration ‘Alacant, San Vicente del Raspeig’ is compliant with collection and treatment requirements. The treatment plant ‘Rincón de León’, applying secondary treatment, also complies since 2012 with all requirements.

There are no details on industrial installations in the question. Those included in Annex I of the Industrial Emissions Directive (5) must have a permit with provisions based on Best Available Techniques (BAT) (6), and emission limit values for polluting substances below the BAT levels. The Commission invites the Honourable Member to liaise with the competent local authorities for questions on permits.

Bathing sites identified in the area under the Bathing Water Directive (7) (Almadrava, l’Albufereta, el Postiguet 1 (or Cocó) and el Postiguet 2), are classified as of excellent quality (bacteriological parameters).

Directive 92/43/EEC on conservation of natural habitats and wild fauna and flora. OJ L 206, 22.7.1992, p. 7-50. Communication EU law: Better results through better application — C/2016/8600, OJ C 18, 19.1.2017, p. 10-20) and Communication COM (2022) 518 final — Enforcing EU law for a Europe that delivers. Ref INFR(2015)2003.

Council Directive 91/271/EEC of 21 May 1991 concerning urban waste-water treatment, OJ L 135, 30.5.1991, p. 40-52. Directive 2010/75/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 24 November 2010 on industrial emissions (integrated pollution prevention and control), OJ L 334, 17.12.2010, p. 17-119.

Best Available Techniques (BAT) means the most effective and advanced techniques, developed on a scale allowing implementation in the relevant industrial sector, under economically and technically viable conditions. Directive 2006/7/EC concerning management of bathing water quality, OJ L 64, 4.3.2006, p. 37-51.
